exposure: Contraction Stress Test (CST) status (negative CST vs. no CST)
outcome: composite neonatal adverse events (Apgar score < 7 at 5 min, umbilical cord pH < 7.1, NICU admission, prolonged neonatal hospitalization, intubation, intraventricular hemorrhage)
combined neonatal and maternal adverse events
cohort: The study included 1688 term singleton pregnancies delivered at a tertiary care center, comprising fetuses with Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR) and Small for Gestational Age (SGA).
finding: A negative Contraction Stress Test (CST) performed prior to labor induction did not reduce the risk of adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes in pregnancies complicated by Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR).
mod_finding: Emergency cesarean delivery rates were comparable between FGR groups (with and without negative CST) but significantly higher than in the SGA group.
birth_weight: FGR was defined as birthweight below the 3rd percentile or prenatally below the 10th percentile with abnormal Doppler findings; SGA was defined as birthweights between the 3rd and 10th percentiles.
